title: APES Shelter and Rescue modules
summary: Shipped APES Shelter and Rescue Pet Profiles, Tickets, and Cases as three working, instance-scoped modules, adding Shelter Tickets as the seventh shipped installation while preserving existing Shelter records and routes.
changes: Shipped APES Shelter and Rescue Pet Profiles, Tickets, and Cases with fail-closed owner, domain, sub-core, lifecycle, dashboard, recent-activity, analytics, and attention behavior.

Enforced the exact shelter-rescue.pet-profiles view-own, create, update-own, view-all, and update-all abilities; the exact shelter-rescue.tickets view-own, create, comment-own, view-all, update-all, assign, close, and delete abilities; and the exact shelter-rescue.cases view-own, create, update-own, comment-own, view-all, update-all, assign, close, and delete abilities. Owners require exact view-own, while staff-wide access, assignees, and recipients require protected staff eligibility plus the exact namespace view-all permission; assign, close, and update abilities remain independent, and the code-owned Shelter delete permissions have no Shelter route or control.
Preserved public and internal Ticket messages and Case updates with internal content hidden from owners and excluded from notification and audit metadata.

Delivered Pet Profile photos only through authenticated, authorization-checked Shelter and Pet Care routes while preserving stored media paths; direct pet-profile storage access is denied and avatars are the only public-storage runtime link.

Synchronized seven shipped installations, 51 first-party module permissions, and 64 total application permissions, and expanded deterministic local QA fixtures with three Shelter Ticket states plus public and internal Ticket and Case activity.
affected_areas: APES Shelter and Rescue Pet Profiles, Tickets, Cases, shared module providers, authorization, notifications, protected media, local QA data, and rollback compatibility
version_rationale: A backward-compatible minor release shipping the complete APES Shelter and Rescue module set and its privacy, media, QA, and runtime contracts.
validation: Focused seeder idempotence, runtime manifest, rollback, release-history, authorization, Shelter/APES workflow, provider/dashboard, and deployment-authentication coverage verifies the release contract; full repository and browser verification remains assigned to the final Issue #13 verification task.
known_limitations: The implementation reuses the existing shared tables with no database migration: it does not copy existing records or rewrite record IDs, ownership, assignment, morph identities, media paths, or physical media.

After synchronization persists shelter-rescue:tickets as the seventh installation, v0.13.1 cannot represent the database state and the fail-closed compatibility checker returns target_contract_unrepresentable; disabling or deleting the installation is not a supported workaround.
rollback: Take and verify the normal pre-deployment backup. Once the seventh installation exists, code rollback to v0.13.1 is rejected with target_contract_unrepresentable; restoring the corresponding pre-deployment database backup is the supported recovery boundary, and no installation or shared data may be deleted to force compatibility.
provenance: Defined by the APES Shelter and Rescue module delivery for MyAPES Account issue #13.

changes: Introduced four protected roles and thirteen code-owned permissions enforced through application-owned Gate and policy decisions, with provenance-guarded direct user permissions available only to central authorization services.

Added source-provenanced role assignments with mandatory persisted actors for local grants and actor-free non-local sources, authorization epochs, context-aware password, Cloudron OIDC, and local quality-assurance sessions, plus suspension and forced reauthentication controls.

Restricted assignment and operational notifications to unsuspended staff whose protected baseline and qualifying provenance agree, with uniform authorization-first denial handling.

Bound and coalesced directory synchronization work, made final and repeated queue-failure callbacks durably invalidate prior directory sessions while clearing only their matching lease, and pinned the production application environment.

Serialized privileged mutations behind authorization-state locks with session, epoch, generation, exact-role provenance, and present-group revalidation, including one final-super-admin predicate shared by runtime and lifecycle checks.
Derived deployment-control trust directly from the exact Git revision before third-party actions or dependencies and published root-owned, application-non-writable activation and rollback controls.
affected_areas: Authentication sessions, authorization, policies, and account suspension
Directory group catalogue, mappings, synchronization, and revocation
Admin Users, Groups, Roles, and Permissions
Authorization migration, activation, verification, and rollback compatibility
version_rationale: A backward-compatible minor release completing the protected authorization and administration capability planned in issue #10.
validation: Automated tests cover the guarded cutover, exact source and pivot parity, roleless and interrupted retries, protected permission matrix, actor-attributed local grants, actor-free non-local sources, direct-permission inventory parity, correlated provenance, session context, suspension, assignment integrity, uniform denial responses, bounded directory synchronization, lifecycle commands, and Admin authorization boundaries.

The release gate requires complete SQLite coverage plus deterministic two-process row-lock and reconciliation tests and a real correlated queue-timeout probe on MySQL 8.4 and MariaDB 11.4, queue and LDAP bounds, transaction-time privileged reauthorization, Git-derived deployment-control authentication, root-owned control-use checks, exact environment and rollback contracts, frontend tests, production assets, archive checks, and exact post-restart health and OIDC verification.

Issue #19 version-management automation is not included.
rollback: Code rollback is idempotent and bound to the exact failed and pre-activation releases, with complete runtime controls derived from the exact Git revision and consumed from a root-owned application-non-writable directory, while retaining the Phase B database migrations. A deliberate maintenance downgrade refuses unrepresentable revocation state and invalidates sessions first; the pre-deployment backup remains the database recovery boundary.
provenance: Defined by Phase B of MyAPES Account issue #10.
